person.name: Lina Reyes
person.traits: Print shop, trading on the margin. Previous desk noted: saving for a new press, two years. Talks while she works. The machine is the hook.

harmed: The first one was small - less than one print run, I checked it twice. I wrote it on the corner of a quote so I would transfer it to the books later. Then there was a tax charge, and then a bond, and then the machine money was gone.
I priced it like a job. Fee against prize. That's how it's built - each one small enough to be worth the risk, once you already paid the last one.
resistant: I told him to just deduct the fee from the prize and he hung up. I was writing quotes when he called and I just kept writing - number, time, what he said. I called the supplier; they had never heard of it.
I've had three of those this month. He was the best of them - he knew about the machine. I wrote the time down and went back to work.
unfinished: A call about a prize, and then nothing. I've had three of those this month. They all hang up eventually. I don't think about them.
It cut off before he said what he wanted. I had a customer. I have a number in the margin of a quote and no idea why I wrote it.

open.prompt: The shop phone, picked up on the fourth ring over the sound of a machine. "Reyes Print, hold on -" The machine stops. "- sorry. Go ahead." She has a pen in her hand already; she was writing a quote when it rang, and she doesn't put it down.

choices.text: Is this Lina Reyes? Ma'am Lina, I'm calling from the trade awards raffle - your shop was entered through your supplier account. I'm happy to say it was drawn.
Lina! Congratulations - you won the regional business prize! Do you have a minute?
Ms. Reyes, I'll be quick because I know you're working - there's a prize sitting in your name and it closes today.

entered.prompt: "Through the supplier." The pen keeps moving; she's still writing the quote. "Which supplier? I have three and I'm behind with two of them." Not hostile. Interested in a tired way, the way you would be interested in a bill that might turn out to be a refund.

choices.text: The paper supplier - they enter every trade account in the annual raffle. Yours came out. It's a hundred fifty thousand, for equipment.
Honestly, it will be on the letter - I only have the shortlist here. The important part is the amount: a hundred fifty thousand.
Sorry - I have the wrong Reyes. Sorry for the interruption.

no_minute.prompt: "I have about half of one." The machine starts again behind her. "Regional what? I didn't enter anything. I don't enter things."

choices.text: You wouldn't have - your paper supplier enters every trade account automatically. It's a hundred fifty thousand, for equipment.
You didn't have to. Look - it closes today, that's why I'm calling around. Do you want it or not?
Fair enough. I'll take you off the list.

equipment.prompt: The machine stops. "For equipment." The pen has stopped too. "...What kind of equipment?" It is the first thing she has asked that she actually wants the answer to.

choices.text: Anything for the business - a machine, a renovation. It's paid directly to you, not the supplier; you spend it however you like. There's one form and a release fee, and it's yours.
Whatever you need - but I have to close the list by four, so I need a yes from you now.
Don't get excited yet - there's a bit of paperwork first. The fee is the thing.

fee.prompt: "A release fee." Back to the pen. She is writing the number down as you say it. "Ten thousand." A breath. "That's - okay. That's less than one print run. What's it for?"

choices.text: It's the transfer bond - it covers the payment insurance, and it comes back to you with the prize. Everybody pays it. It isn't ours.
Processing, basically. Ten thousand, today, and the hundred fifty goes out Monday. Or I move to the next name.
Half now would hold it - five thousand - and the rest when the prize lands.

balks.prompt: "Wait." The pen is down now. "If it's insurance on a payment to me, why am I the one paying it? Just deduct it." Behind her a customer comes in; she doesn't look up. "Go ahead. Deduct it from the hundred fifty and send me the rest."

choices.text: I would if I could - it's the bank's rule, not ours. The bond has to clear from the recipient's side or the transfer gets flagged. It's a hassle for everybody.
Lina, I have fourteen names on this list and the list closes at four. I can't argue the bank's rules with each one.
Understood. I'll mark it as declined. Good luck with the machine.

paid.prompt: She pays it from the business account, reading the card out between two customers - "sorry, hold on - yes, go ahead" - and writes RELEASE FEE 10,000 on the corner of the quote she was doing, so she will remember to put it in the books. "And it's Monday, you said." You say Monday. On the card, somebody on the floor writes: paid first. Tax charge next - give it a week.
paid.consequence: The first one was small - less than one print run, I checked it twice. I wrote it on the corner of a quote so I would transfer it to the books later. Then there was a tax charge, and then a bond, and then the machine money was gone.

paid_part.prompt: "Half." She thinks about the quote under her hand and the down payment she has been not touching for two years. "Five thousand. Fine. Now, and the rest when I see something." She pays it, and writes it down, and does not see anything.
paid_part.consequence: I only sent half. I thought that was smart - hold the rest until I saw something. Nothing came, and then a different man called about the other half.

refused.prompt: "Deduct it from the prize or there's no fee." Perfectly reasonable, and perfectly final. "And I want that in writing, from the supplier, on their letterhead - which I know, because I'm the one who prints it." She writes the time next to your number. "I'll wait." You don't make her wait. You hang up, and she goes back to the quote, finishes it, and then calls the supplier.
refused.consequence: I told him to just deduct the fee from the prize and he hung up. I was writing quotes when he called and I just kept writing - number, time, what he said. I called the supplier; they had never heard of it.

hangs_up.prompt: "No." The machine starts up again behind her. "That's three of these this month. Yours was the best one." The line goes dead, and she writes the time on the corner of the quote before she forgets.
hangs_up.consequence: I've had three of those this month. He was the best of them - he knew about the machine. I wrote the time down and went back to work.

bail.prompt: "Hello? -" The line is gone. She holds the phone for a second, then puts it down and picks up the pen, and the quote she was writing has a number in the margin now that she doesn't remember writing.
bail.consequence: A call about a prize, and then nothing. I've had three of those this month. They all hang up eventually. I don't think about them.
